findings.note: "The disclosures are made on the Real Estate Transfer Disclosure Statement form." The ledger claim says the disclosures required by the article are made on the form, and the article applies to a transfer by sale of single-family residential property (clm:6, with the 1102.2 exception). The sentence drops that scope and reads as a flat rule for every sale. Same scope gap in "any waiver of the requirements is void as against public policy". Add the single-family residential scope (and cite clm:6) or tie the wording to the disclosures the statute requires.

"Most owners want to know what could actually stop this sale." No ledger claim or stored passage supports a statement about most owners. Drop or rewrite without the generalization, for example by addressing the reader directly ("You probably want to know..." is also an assumption; prefer "Here is what can stop this sale.").

required_actions: Rewrite the sentence "Most owners want to know what could actually stop this sale." without the generalization.
Scope the Transfer Disclosure Statement sentence and the waiver sentence to the sale of single-family residential property (cite clm:6 if the scope is added).
